1.name: Jaylen Summers
1.about: The projected top pick, Summers pairs elite athleticism and a 6’11” wingspan with relentless downhill pressure. He blows by defenders at will, finishes through contact, and flashes lead-guard instincts, giving him true franchise-cornerstone upside.

2.name: Trey James
2.about: In the mix for the top pick, James is the draft’s premier shooter and a lethal isolation scorer. He creates space with craft and balance, punishes switches from deep or mid-range, and projects as a go-to offensive engine.

3.name: Nicola Mancini
3.about: Recruited out of Italy, Mancini is one of the draft’s best perimeter defenders, pairing discipline and anticipation with a polished mid-range game. He controls tempo, disrupts opposing guards, and projects as a high-level two-way combo guard.

4.name: Adam Riley
4.about: The nation’s top-ranked recruit, Riley is a dominant defensive anchor with elite rim protection instincts. His offensive game is budding, showing touch around the basket and improving feel, while his defensive impact projects him as a long-term cornerstone.

5.name: Saúl Segura
5.about: The top international prospect on the board, Segura is a polished scoring wing with elite mid-range feel. He wins with footwork, touch, and poise, reading defenses comfortably and projecting as a pro-ready offensive option on the wing.

6.name: Taji Anikulapo-Kuti
6.about: A punishing, physical defender with an immense wingspan, Anikulapo-Kuti overwhelms opponents with strength and reach. He disrupts passing lanes, bodies wings and forwards, and sets a defensive tone as a high-impact stopper.

7.name: Sincere Johnston
7.about: College basketball’s most improved player, Johnston is a tough, confident shot-creator who thrives in isolation. He scores through contact, uses refined footwork to create space, and projects as a reliable half-court option with versatility.

8.name: Joshua Boston
8.about: A five-star recruit out of Atlanta, Boston is an explosive downhill wing who attacks defenders with speed and bounce. He pressures the rim relentlessly, finishes above traffic, and projects as a high-energy scorer capable of shifting momentum.

9.name: Ismaël Aït Salah
9.about: A high-upside international forward with strong defensive instincts, Aït Salah is an underrated passer who makes sharp reads on the move. He defends multiple positions, finishes in transition, and flashes playmaking feel that elevates his projection.

10.name: Riley Jamison
10.about: A top-10 recruit nationally, Jamison projects as a high-upside guard despite his size, driven by steady offensive production at Arizona. He spaces the floor, creates in pick-and-rolls, and provides reliable shot-making and playmaking.

11.name: Isaiah Bailey
11.about: A five-star recruit with elite high school pedigree, Bailey brings strength and deep shooting range to the wing. Comfortable scoring through contact, he thrives in isolation and projects as a confident three-level self-creator at the next level.

12.name: Terrence James
12.about: One of two five-star recruits at Tennessee, James impacts winning as a disciplined 3-and-D wing. He spaces the floor reliably, defends with physicality, and fits cleanly into structured lineups as a dependable two-way contributor.

13.name: Bernard Johnson
13.about: After transferring from Georgia, Johnson provides polished interior scoring and physicality. He thrives on the block, finishes through contact, flashes face-up touch, and projects as a dependable frontcourt scorer with developing range.

14.name: Chancellor Harris
14.about: Built like a modern combo guard, Harris offers excellent size and a high floor. He scores downhill, defends multiple positions, limits mistakes, and projects as a reliable do-it-all guard with few glaring weaknesses.

15.name: Jaylen Simmons
15.about: A left-handed, high-energy guard, Simmons pairs confident perimeter shooting with aggressive ball pressure. He hunts shots, disrupts passing lanes, and brings pace on both ends, projecting as a spark plug guard with developing offensive consistency.

16.name: Darius Hall
16.about: Just 18 years old, Hall is one of the youngest prospects in the draft and already an explosive interior defender. He protects the rim, finishes as a rim runner, and offers high-upside defensive impact as his offense develops.

17.name: Mark Bolton
17.about: As a classic Duke big, Bolton relies on footwork, strength, and touch to score inside. He finishes through contact, rebounds consistently, and projects as a reliable frontcourt scorer whose value comes from feel and consistency.

18.name: Terrance Edwards
18.about: Comfortable spacing the floor, Edwards stretches defenses with deep range and quick release. He thrives spotting up or trailing in transition, competes defensively, and projects as a reliable shooting forward in modern lineups.

19.name: Kason Smith
19.about: Known for his composure, Smith operates as a steady table-setter who values efficiency. He reads defenses, delivers timely passes, and knocks down open looks, projecting as a dependable secondary guard with strong feel and control.

20.name: Jack Rice
20.about: A sophomore and one of the draft’s best spot-up shooters, Rice brings deep range and confidence. He punishes help defenses, adds isolation scoring late in possessions, and projects as a spacing forward with situational creation value.

21.name: Aviel Elbaz
21.about: Coming from Israel, Elbaz is a crafty combo guard who logged meaningful minutes as an international prospect. He balances scoring and playmaking, reads the floor well in structured offenses, and projects as a steady offensive connector with pro experience.

22.name: Dave Mosley
22.about: As a sophomore, Mosley brings physical interior presence and toughness to the frontcourt. He thrives bullying defenders on the block, cleaning the glass, and providing reliable interior scoring, projecting as a rotational big who impacts games through strength and effort.

23.name: Semaj Jenkins
23.about: Despite being undersized, Jenkins consistently holds his own against bigger players. His 6’11” wingspan fuels ball-hawking defense, physicality, and disruption, allowing him to play above his size and project as a versatile defensive forward.

24.name: Xavion Booker
24.about: A five-star recruit with a legendary high school mixtape, Booker brings confidence and flair to the backcourt. He thrives in the mid-range, plays with swagger, and projects as a shot-making guard whose creativity translates to high-level scoring upside.

25.name: Jadyn Mora
25.about: One of the top upperclassmen in the class, Mora enters as a seasoned senior scorer. He thrives creating offense in isolation, punishes mismatches, and offers late-clock shot-making, projecting as a reliable scoring guard with experience-driven poise.

26.name: Kavon Williams
26.about: Using his long wingspan to smother defenders, Williams thrives as a disruptive two-way wing. He pressures ball-handlers, attacks downhill when lanes open, and projects as a versatile defender whose length drives his impact on both ends.

27.name: Cam Lee
27.about: Serving as Oklahoma’s offensive focal point, Lee consistently produces despite standing just 6’0”. He controls tempo, thrives in the mid-range, and proves size isn’t a limiter, projecting as one of college basketball’s most dependable scorers.

28.name: Dustin Anderson
28.about: A high-flying slasher with a massive social media following, Anderson has become a fan favorite. He attacks defenders with confidence, thrives in the mid-range, and marks the second straight Oklahoma player selected on the board.

29.name: Iago Barcellos
29.about: Hailing from Brazil, Barcellos is a two-way international forward who brings athletic interior play. He finishes above the rim, competes defensively, and flashes stretch potential, projecting as a developmental big with modern versatility.

30.name: Mathys Moreau
30.about: A lightweight center with perimeter touch, Moreau adds spacing value as a stretch five. He knocks down open threes, moves well for his size, and projects as a floor-spacing big whose offensive skill offsets physical limitations.

31.name: Mahlik Joseph
31.about: Built as a sturdy two-way guard, Joseph plays through contact and brings downhill pressure on both ends. He attacks gaps, competes defensively, and offers rotation value as a strength-based guard whose impact comes from effort and reliability.

32.name: Niklas Helm
32.about: Functioning best in defined roles, Helm impacts games as a mobile rim runner and lob threat. He moves well defensively, plays within structure, and projects as a developmental international big who adds vertical spacing and team defense.

33.name: Andrew Bolden Jr.
33.about: Defense drives Bolden’s value as a physical, assignment-ready forward. He pressures ball-handlers, anticipates passing lanes, and embraces tough matchups, projecting as a situational stopper whose offense stays within the flow of the game.

34.name: Kristiāns Lapiņš
34.about: Size and rim protection define Lapiņš’ profile as an international center. He alters shots, competes on the glass, and flashes short-range touch, projecting as a depth big whose value is rooted in interior defense and physical presence.

35.name: Jabari Henry
35.about: Energy and athleticism shape Henry’s frontcourt impact. He finishes plays above the rim, runs the floor hard, and rebounds through traffic, projecting as a developmental big whose utility comes from rim running and physical activity.

36.name: Justinas Jakčinskas
36.about: Still early in his development, Jakčinskas offers length, mobility, and rim-running ability. He impacts games defensively and as a finisher, projecting as a long-term project big with rotational upside anchored in defense.

37.name: Nicholas Falk
37.about: Experience and shooting anchor Falk’s appeal as a depth wing. He spaces the floor with confident spot-up range, understands positioning, and projects as a rotational shooter whose value comes from gravity and lineup flexibility.

38.name: Luke Causey
38.about: Spacing-oriented lineups benefit most from Causey’s skill set. He provides floor-spacing, offensive feel, and solid movement for his size, projecting as a situational stretch big rather than a traditional interior presence.

39.name: Cody Meadows
39.about: Youth and shooting upside headline Meadows’ projection as a developmental wing. He competes defensively, plays within structure, and knocks down open looks, offering long-term rotation potential tied to perimeter growth.

40.name: Mark Smiley
40.about: Scoring instincts define Smiley’s role projection. He’s comfortable creating offense in limited usage, attacking mismatches late in possessions, and projects as a bench scorer whose value depends on rhythm and situational deployment.

41.name: Miles Gibson
41.about: Built around strength and mass, Gibson operates as a post-oriented interior presence. He carves out space, finishes through contact, and controls the glass, projecting as a depth big whose value comes from physicality rather than offensive versatility.

42.name: Davonte Huntley
42.about: Comfortably operating in the mid-post, Huntley provides interior scoring and cleanup value. He finishes plays efficiently, rebounds his area, and plays within structure, projecting as a rotational frontcourt option built on strength and reliability.

43.name: Alex Humphrey
43.about: Shooting anchors Humphrey’s projection as a spacing wing. He hunts threes confidently, understands off-ball movement, and fits best as a floor spacer whose value comes from shooting gravity and veteran composure rather than on-ball creation.

44.name: Alex Mahon
44.about: Creative shot-making defines Mahon’s offensive profile as a perimeter scorer. He stretches defenses with shooting range, adds secondary creation, and projects as a situational wing whose offensive value depends on efficiency and shot selection.

45.name: Samy Delaunay
45.about: Explosiveness and athletic tools headline Delaunay’s appeal as a young international wing. He attacks downhill, finishes above the rim, and brings defensive activity, projecting as a developmental scorer whose impact grows with structure and refinement.

46.name: Kevin Tyson
46.about: Length and athleticism give Tyson value as a slashing wing. He pressures defenses off the bounce, competes defensively, and projects as a developmental rotation piece whose role centers on energy, transition play, and physical tools.

47.name: Jake Smith
47.about: Rebounding and interior toughness drive Smith’s value as a traditional center. He hunts boards, finishes around the rim, and provides physical presence, projecting as a depth big whose impact is tied to effort and interior work.

48.name: Tristian Roach
48.about: Physical downhill play defines Roach’s role as a power wing. He attacks mismatches, absorbs contact, and defends with effort, projecting as a situational rotation option whose value comes from strength, motor, and versatility.

49.name: Aaron Carrillo
49.about: Athleticism shapes Carrillo’s projection as an energy big. He plays above the rim, runs the floor hard, and finishes with force, projecting as a developmental frontcourt piece whose impact comes from activity and vertical pressure.

50.name: Matthias Hamilton
50.about: Perimeter shooting drives Hamilton’s appeal as a spacing forward. He stretches defenses with spot-up range, plays within his role, and projects as a rotational shooter whose value comes from size, shooting, and lineup fit.

51.name: Jonathan Ford
51.about: Explosive athleticism defines Ford’s appeal as a young guard prospect. He attacks downhill, elevates quickly at the rim, and brings defensive activity, projecting as a developmental rotation guard whose value hinges on efficiency and decision-making.

52.name: Danny Schneider
52.about: Experience and craft shape Schneider’s profile as an older frontcourt option. He finishes plays with touch, moves well for his size, and projects as a depth big whose offensive value comes from feel rather than physical dominance.

53.name: Brayan Hunt
53.about: Shooting anchors Hunt’s role projection as a spacing wing. He hunts perimeter looks confidently, plays within structure, and fits best as a rotational shooter whose value comes from floor spacing and off-ball awareness.

54.name: Eric Welch
54.about: Left-handed shooting gives Welch intrigue as a perimeter role guard. He stretches defenses from deep, competes defensively, and projects as a rotation piece whose offensive value depends on shot consistency and secondary playmaking.

55.name: Julian McGhee
55.about: Physical downhill play drives McGhee’s two-way value. He attacks gaps aggressively, finishes above the rim, and defends with effort, projecting as a rotational forward whose impact is tied to energy and athletic pressure.

56.name: Bruno Correa
56.about: Strength and physicality define Correa’s scoring approach as an international wing. He thrives bullying defenders inside the arc, embraces contact, and projects as a developmental scorer whose role grows with improved perimeter efficiency.

57.name: Abdoulaye Saint-Laurent
57.about: Length and rim protection highlight Saint-Laurent’s defensive appeal. He alters shots, finishes plays above the rim, and flashes stretch potential, projecting as a developmental big whose value is rooted in defensive impact and vertical spacing.

58.name: Makai Bridges
58.about: Versatility and toughness shape Bridges’ profile as a combo guard. He scores comfortably from the mid-range, defends with length, and projects as a rotation piece whose value comes from two-way reliability rather than high usage.

59.name: Rickey Britt
59.about: Shooting and playmaking give Britt situational value as a depth guard. He spaces the floor, creates off the bounce in short stretches, and projects as a developmental rotation option whose role depends on efficiency and defensive growth.

60.name: Joey Anderson
60.about: Offensive skill defines Anderson’s appeal as a frontcourt option. He scores comfortably on the block, flashes stretch ability, and projects as a depth big whose value comes from scoring versatility rather than defensive anchoring.
